findings: Field strength alone does nothing for the drawn topology: x4 the field leaves the struck share at 0.67 (x1: 0.67), because magnetised debris from an on-axis burn follows the same field lines at any strength.

Topology and position decide it: moving the burn 4 m aft of its drawn point lowers the struck share to 0.46, and with closure rings at four times their current share to 0.21. Strong closure with the burn at or forward of its drawn point seals the nozzle instead: 5 of 32 geometries strike every debris ion (hit 1.0, no thrust).

Best geometry for the design target, mirror4|4|1: 0.94 MN for four engines (drawn 0.44 MN), 8,452 km/s, heat 1,967x the radiator share (drawn 2,188x). Interception is a thrust lever, not a heat lever: X-rays carry most of the heat.
Early extraction (80 % of the product energy out of the target) cuts the heat to 304x but the thrust to 0.36 MN: fast products carry energy, not momentum. It is a heat lever, not a thrust lever.
No case closes. The thrust-heat frontier runs from 300x at 0.34 MN to 7,869x at 3.78 MN; the mission needs 21.8 MN at 1x.

Limits: vacuum test particles from an on-axis point (24 directions per species, struck-share error about +/-0.10); the X-ray pickup is the drawn engine's for every geometry (not recomputed for a moved burn, OPEN); coil masses scale with capture current and are relative only; plasma expansion, detachment and collective effects are OPEN.
